findings.claim: Ruling (b) at CONTEXT.md:57 sets the guard's round to the round under repair, so `record` writes `<slug>.ruling.N.txt` for that uncited plan. That marks round N tried (:98), and `repairs` counts only cite lines for rounds above the latest tried round (:119), so every later failed repair of plan N goes uncounted and the guard can never fire again.
findings.failure_scenario: Plan 3 holds a marker that never resolves. After 5 repair-only iterations, guard (b) asks the owner and `record` writes ruling.3.txt, so round 3 now counts as tried. Plan 3 is still uncited, so `state` returns round 3, owed defense (:106, :109), and the defense keeps editing plan 3. Each `cite` run appends to cite.3.txt, but 3 is not above the latest tried round (3), so `repairs` stays 0. `stretch` adds no ask: it counts tried rounds above `since`=3, and under (b) it is still read only from a review written in the iteration, which no repair-only iteration writes. No tried round is added, so `run_rounds` never reaches CAP. The Opus defense repairs up to 200 times and the loop ends on `max_iterations` with no second ask, which is the G-54 defect left standing after the first ruling.

findings.claim: When the defense does fix the plan after a guard ruling, ruling (b) makes the repaired plan unreachable. Round N has a ruling and therefore counts as tried, so once it is cited `state` moves to round N+1, owed defense. The prosecutor never tries plan N, and the defense spends an extra Opus turn rewriting it as N+1.
findings.failure_scenario: Guard asks on uncited plan 3 and `record` writes ruling.3.txt. Next iteration the defense fixes plan 3 and `cite` resolves it. `ready` then reads plan 3 as cited and tried (ruling exists), so it returns round 4, owed defense (:106, :109). `screen` and the prosecutor are skipped, `case` returns none, and the next iteration runs a full defense turn to write plan 4 as a copy of the already repaired plan 3. That is a token-waste defect under CLAUDE.md 1.3, repeated on every guard ask.
